name: WebSphere eXtreme Scale
tagline: IBM's Java in-memory data grid for caching, HTTP sessions and partitioned object storage; still patched.
description: IBM WebSphere eXtreme Scale (WXS) is an elastic in-memory data grid for Java: data is held as key-addressed objects in maps, partitioned across many JVMs with synchronous or asynchronous replica shards, and accessed through its ObjectGrid APIs, a dynamic cache provider for WebSphere and Liberty, or HTTP session replication. Loaders can read through and write behind to a backing relational database. It is a mainstay of large WebSphere estates in banking, retail and telecom. IBM keeps it alive: version 8.6.2 (September 2025) added Java 11 and 17 support with a new installation model, and fix pack 8.6.2.2 followed in June 2026.

pricing.notes: Licensed through IBM, typically per processor value unit.

scale.notes: Grids partition data across many container JVMs with primary and replica shards for failover.

strengths: Proven at large scale inside WebSphere and Liberty environments
Automatic partitioning, replica placement and failover across JVMs
Drop-in dynamic cache and HTTP session store for WebSphere applications
Read-through and write-behind loaders keep a backing database in sync
weaknesses: Java-centric and tightly coupled to the IBM WebSphere ecosystem
Roadmap is maintenance-oriented; little new functionality beyond Java currency
useCases: HTTP session replication for WebSphere/Liberty clusters
Caching in front of DB2 or Oracle for high-traffic Java apps
Partitioned in-memory object storage for transaction processing
